standard_prerequisites.name: Reduction from complexes to a sheaf
standard_prerequisites.statement: A complex K in D^+(X_etale) is represented by a bounded below complex of abelian sheaves, and the sheaf case applied degreewise together with Leray's acyclicity lemma gives the complex case (Derived Categories, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction at source lines 1234-1243.

standard_prerequisites.name: The comparison lemma for the fppf topology
standard_prerequisites.statement: a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = F and R^i epsilon_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}F) = 0 for i > 0 (the author's lemma-comparison-fppf-etale, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives the identity and one vanishing at source lines 1246-1253.

standard_prerequisites.name: Descent along the projection to the small etale site
standard_prerequisites.statement: R^j pi_{X,*}(pi_X^{-1}F) = 0 for j > 0 (the author's lemma-cohomological-descent-etale, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the other vanishing in the Leray decomposition at source lines 1256-1257.

standard_prerequisites.name: The relative Leray spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Leray spectral sequence for a composite functor, used for a_X = epsilon_X o pi_X (Cohomology on Sites, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It combines the two vanishing statements at source lines 1249-1251.

core_obligations: Reduce to a single abelian sheaf: represent K by a bounded below complex, apply the sheaf case degreewise, and use Leray's acyclicity lemma (source lines 1234-1243).
Sheaf case, first identity: a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = F is the second part of the chapter's fppf comparison lemma (source lines 1245-1247).

Sheaf case, vanishing: decompose a_X = epsilon_X o pi_X, use the relative Leray spectral sequence, the vanishing R^i epsilon_{X,*}(a_X^{-1}F) = 0 from the fppf comparison lemma, and the vanishing R^j pi_{X,*}(pi_X^{-1}F) = 0 from the descent lemma (source lines 1247-1258).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the complex case to one abelian sheaf, using the degreewise sheaf case and Leray's acyclicity lemma.
Use the fppf comparison lemma for a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = F and reduce to the vanishing.
Combine the relative Leray spectral sequence with the two vanishing statements for epsilon_{X,*} and pi_{X,*}.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cohomological-descent-etale-fppf at source lines 1218-1229: for K in D^+(X_etale) - with no torsion hypothesis, unlike the ph statement - the maps pi_X^{-1}K -> R epsilon_{X,*}a_X^{-1}K and K -> R a_{X,*}a_X^{-1}K are isomorphisms. The author's proof at source lines 1231-1259 proves the second statement only (noting the first is easier and identical in method), reduces from a bounded below complex to a single abelian sheaf by the sheaf case degreewise together with Leray's acyclicity lemma (a cross-chapter pointer), and then proves the sheaf case from the two parts of the chapter's fppf comparison lemma (retained as context), the relative Leray spectral sequence for a_X = epsilon_X o pi_X (a second pointer), the vanishing of the higher direct images of epsilon_{X,*} on a_X^{-1}F, and the vanishing of R^j pi_{X,*} on pi_X^{-1}F supplied by the chapter's descent lemma (also retained as context). The counted argument is a complete two-stage reduction whose in-chapter ingredients are available inside the package.
